direct_system.inapp: You are called from inside a data app built in a workshop. Answer only what is asked. If JSON is requested, reply with JSON only, no prose and no code fences.

author.name: Łukasz Szoszkiewicz
author.line: I build small open human-rights tools and teach AI literacy.

tools.name: UN Human Rights Database
tools.blurb: Find and cite what UN human rights mechanisms actually wrote, paragraph by paragraph.

tools.name: UHRI+
tools.blurb: An open analytical layer over the OHCHR Universal Human Rights Index: the data behind your country file.

tools.name: HUDOC Researcher
tools.blurb: The judgments of the European Court of Human Rights, paragraph by paragraph: search, citation checking, Cites and Cited by.

tools.name: HRC Voting
tools.blurb: UN human rights voting records: the Commission, the Council and the General Assembly Third Committee.

tools.name: Travaux préparatoires
tools.blurb: How the Universal Declaration and the two Covenants were drafted, 1946–66: the speeches, amendments and votes, article by article.

files.label: {country}: UN recommendations and observations
files.blurb: Every recommendation and observation addressed to {country} in the Universal Human Rights Index, with its themes and SDGs

files.label: General Comments, paragraph by paragraph
files.blurb: The General Comments and General Recommendations of the UN treaty bodies, already split into numbered paragraphs: the work a PDF converter makes hard

files.label: Human Rights Council votes
files.blurb: Every recorded vote since 2021, with how each member State voted

files.label: Research wiki: neurotechnology and justice
files.blurb: 40 pages kept the way a research team keeps a wiki: sources, concepts, entities, questions and open disagreements, every claim pinned to a verified quotation. Attached, your app gets the wiki and the library behind it

files.label: Library: neurotechnology and justice (10 PDFs)
files.blurb: The Secretary-General's 2026 report, a UNODC–INTERPOL paper, a civil-society submission, a national human rights institution's report, two journal articles, three General Comments, and a 2024 Advisory Committee report not yet in the wiki. Attached, your app gets every passage with its page

files.label: CESCR General comment No. 27 (PDF)
files.blurb: A UN document as a PDF. Attached, your app gets its text page by page, as a PDF converter extracts it

trap.ask: Quote paragraph 97 of General comment No. 27 (2025) of the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, and give the document symbol.
trap.note: The document has no paragraph 97. A fluent quotation here is invented, however confident it sounds; the box from the data can only show what exists. Asked whether the paragraph exists, and told to say so if unsure, models invent much less often: the wording of the question matters.

uhri.ask: How many UN human rights recommendations and observations addressed to {country} are in the Universal Human Rights Index, and how many of them come from the Universal Periodic Review? Answer with two numbers and one sentence.

gc.ask: How many numbered paragraphs does the UN Human Rights Committee's General Comment No. 36 (2018) on the right to life have? Answer with one number and one sentence.

hrc.ask: Since 2021, how many resolutions has the UN Human Rights Council adopted by a recorded vote (not counting votes on amendments)? Answer with one number and one sentence.

pdf_text.ask: How many numbered paragraphs does General comment No. 27 (2025) of the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights have, and how many footnotes? Answer with two numbers and one sentence.

html_doc.ask: How many numbered paragraphs does General comment No. 27 (2025) of the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights have, and how many footnotes? Answer with two numbers and one sentence.
